subproblem.title: Weighted approximate tangent spaces exist a.e. on a countably rectifiable set (Simon 3, Theorem 1.9 via Remark 1.8(1), localized to U)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, M ⊆ U Hⁿ-measurable (null-measurable for μHE[n]) and countably n-rectifiable, and θ : ℝ^P → ℝ with θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M and θ Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U. Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there is an n-dimensional linear subspace V of ℝ^P which is the approximate tangent space of M at x with respect to θ (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x V): dim V = n and lim_{r↓0} ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y) θ(x + r y) dHⁿ(y) = θ(x) ∫_V f dHⁿ for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), where η_{x,r}(y) = r^{-1}(y − x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ), IsOpen U → M ⊆ U → NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl P)) → CountablyRectifiable (m + 1) M → (∀ x ∈ M, 0 < θ x) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K) (μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl P))) → ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), ∃ V : Submodule ℝ (Eucl P), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt (m + 1) M θ x V
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 3, Theorem 1.9 (p. 75): 'Suppose M ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} is Hⁿ-measurable and θ is a positive Hⁿ-measurable function on M with ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for each compact K ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ}. Then M is countably n-rectifiable ⟺ M has an approximate tangent space T_xM with respect to θ for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M'. Simon deduces this from Theorem 1.6 via Remark 1.8(1). We follow the printed proofs of 1.6 '⇒' (pp. 71-72) and of Remark 1.8(1), the latter using Lusin's Theorem 1.17 and 3.6 of Ch. 1. There are three adaptations.
 (a) θ is only integrable on compact subsets of U; this is handled by localization (step 2).
 (b) The printed proof of 1.6 '⇒' covers M by embedded C¹ submanifolds (Lemma 1.2). The 'only if' part of Lemma 1.2 rests on the C¹ approximation theorem (Ch. 2, 1.5), and it is not in the pinned library: SimonGMT Chapter03/SubmanifoldCover.lean proves only the converse. Step 4 does not use Lemma 1.2. It cuts the Lipschitz parametrizations of Definition 1.1 into bi-Lipschitz pieces and computes the blow-ups with the injective and linear area formulas, using only proved, axiom-checked library results (listed in step 4). The density argument of the printed proof (the Upper Density Theorem 3.6 of Ch. 1) is kept.
 (c) The case P = n needs no separate treatment, and P < n is vacuous (step 1).

1. Dimension. If P < n then Hⁿ ≡ 0 on ℝ^P (ℝ^P has Hausdorff dimension P < n), so Hⁿ⌞M = 0 and the statement is vacuous. Assume P ≥ n.

2. Localization. Let W_q (q ∈ ℕ) be open sets with closure(W_q) compact and ⊆ U and ⋃_q W_q = U, and let M_q := M ∩ W_q (Hⁿ-measurable). θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M_q ⊆ M ∩ closure(W_q), hence on M_q ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P. For x ∈ M_q, (M_q, θ) has approximate tangent space V at x iff (M, θ) has: if f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), spt f ⊆ B_R(0) and 0 < r < dist(x, ℝ^P∖W_q)/R, then every y ∈ η_{x,r}(M)∖η_{x,r}(M_q) has x + r y ∈ M∖W_q, so r|y| ≥ dist(x, ℝ^P∖W_q) > rR and f(y) = 0; therefore ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y) θ(x + r y) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{η_{x,r}(M_q)} f(y) θ(x + r y) dHⁿ(y) for all small r > 0, and the limits as r ↓ 0 coincide. Since M = ⋃_q M_q and a countable union of null sets is null, it suffices to prove the theorem for each M_q. Fix q and write M for M_q: now θ ∈ L¹(Hⁿ⌞M), θ > 0 on M, and M is Hⁿ-measurable and countably n-rectifiable.

3. Remark 1.8(1). Hⁿ⌞M is σ-finite: M = ⋃_k {x ∈ M : θ(x) > 1/k} and Hⁿ({θ > 1/k} ∩ M) ≤ k ∫_M θ dHⁿ < ∞. By Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17) applied to θ on these sets of finite measure, and the pasting lemma for finitely many closed sets, there is an increasing sequence of closed sets M^{(j)} ⊆ M, compact because M ⊆ W_q is bounded (Lusin: SimonGMT IsBorelRegularOuterMeasure.simon_theorem_1_17; θ|M is Hⁿ-Carathéodory-measurable, being Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. equal to a Borel function), with Hⁿ(M∖⋃_j M^{(j)}) = 0 and θ|M^{(j)} continuous; then θ ≥ c_j > 0 on M^{(j)} and Hⁿ(M^{(j)}) ≤ c_j^{-1} ∫_M θ < ∞. Let μ := θ Hⁿ⌞M (a finite Borel regular measure). By the Upper Density Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6), applied to μ and the μ-measurable set M∖M^{(j)} of finite μ-measure, there is an Hⁿ-null set E_j such that Θ*ⁿ(μ, M∖M^{(j)}, x) = 0 for every x ∈ M^{(j)}∖E_j.

4. Theorem 1.6 '⇒' for M′ := M^{(j)}, via Lipschitz parametrizations. M′ is compact, Hⁿ(M′) < ∞, and M′ is countably n-rectifiable as a subset of M. Claim: there is an Hⁿ-null set Z_j ⊆ ℝ^P such that every x ∈ M′∖Z_j has two properties. First, there is an n-dimensional subspace L_x with lim_{λ↓0}∫_{η_{x,λ}(M′)}f dHⁿ = ∫_{L_x}f dHⁿ for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) (Definition 1.4 of Ch. 3). Second, Hⁿ(M′ ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ C_xρⁿ for all small ρ > 0.
 Library results used, all axiom-checked with only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound:
 - Rademacher's theorem (Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt);
 - the null image of the critical set (SimonGMT area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero);
 - the countable partition into pieces on which a map is close to a linear map (Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt);
 - Borel measurability of injective continuous images of Borel sets (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn);
 - the injective area formula for Lipschitz maps ℝⁿ → ℝ^P (SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn);
 - the linear area formula (SimonGMT linear_area_formula);
 - Lebesgue's differentiation theorem on ℝⁿ (Mathlib IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub);
 - the upper density theorem (SimonGMT simon_theorem_3_6).
 (a) Parametrizations. By Definition 1.1 (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable), M′ ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_iF_i(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and each F_i : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P Lipschitz.
 (b) Regular parts. Fix i. Let D_i := {b ∈ ℝⁿ : F_i is differentiable at b} and R_i := {b ∈ D_i : dF_i(b) is injective}. Both are Borel: D_i by measurableSet_of_differentiableAt, and R_i because injectivity of dF_i(b) is equivalent to the nonvanishing of the Borel function areaJacobianAt F_i.
 By Rademacher, Lⁿ(ℝⁿ∖D_i) = 0, so Hⁿ(F_i(ℝⁿ∖D_i)) ≤ Lip(F_i)ⁿLⁿ(ℝⁿ∖D_i) = 0. Also Hⁿ(F_i(D_i∖R_i)) = 0 by area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero.
 For an injective linear map A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P let κ(A) := min_{|c|=1}|Ac| > 0. Apply exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt to F_i on R_i, with derivative dF_i, and with r(A) := κ(A)/2 for injective A and r(A) := 1 otherwise. It gives pairwise disjoint Borel sets t_{i,l} with R_i ⊆ ⋃_lt_{i,l} and linear maps A_{i,l} such that |F_i(b) − F_i(b′) − A_{i,l}(b − b′)| ≤ r(A_{i,l})|b − b′| for b, b′ ∈ R_i ∩ t_{i,l}. Moreover, if R_i ≠ ∅, then A_{i,l} = dF_i(y) for some y ∈ R_i, so A_{i,l} is injective. Hence on S_{i,l} := R_i ∩ t_{i,l}, |F_i(b) − F_i(b′)| ≥ (κ(A_{i,l})/2)|b − b′|.
 (c) Re-indexing. Discard the pairs with S_{i,l} = ∅. For every remaining pair R_i ≠ ∅, so A_{i,l} = dF_i(y) for some y ∈ R_i is injective; put κ := κ(A_{i,l})/2 > 0. Enumerate the remaining countably many pairs (F_i, S_{i,l}) as (G_p, S_p)_{p≥1}, with κ_p the corresponding κ. Each G_p : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P is Lipschitz (constant L_p), and each S_p is Borel. G_p is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of S_p, and |G_p(b) − G_p(b′)| ≥ κ_p|b − b′| for b, b′ ∈ S_p, with κ_p > 0. Moreover M′ ⊆ N ∪ ⋃_pG_p(S_p), where N := M₀ ∪ ⋃_iF_i(ℝⁿ∖R_i) has Hⁿ(N) = 0. Each G_p(S_p) is Borel (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).
 (d) Disjoint pieces. Let M′_p := (M′ ∩ G_p(S_p))∖⋃_{q<p}G_q(S_q) and A_p := S_p ∩ G_p^{−1}(M′_p); both are Borel. G_p maps A_p bijectively onto M′_p, the M′_p are pairwise disjoint, and M′∖⋃_pM′_p ⊆ N.
 Let J_p(b) := areaJacobianAt G_p b = √det(dG_p(b)*dG_p(b)), a Borel function. On S_p, 0 < J_p ≤ L_pⁿ: J_p(b) is the product of the n singular values of dG_p(b), each at most ‖dG_p(b)‖ ≤ L_p, and J_p > 0 because dG_p(b) is injective (areaJacobianAt_eq_zero_iff_not_injective). By the injective area formula (weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn, applied to the positive and negative parts of g), every bounded Borel g on ℝ^P satisfies
 ∫_{M′_p}g dHⁿ = ∫_{A_p}J_p(b)g(G_p(b))db.
 (e) Good points. Let h_p := 1_{A_p}J_p, which is bounded and Borel. By Lebesgue's differentiation theorem, for Lⁿ-a.e. b ∈ A_p we have λ^{−n}∫_{B̄_λ(b)}|h_p(b′) − J_p(b)|db′ → 0 as λ ↓ 0. Let A_p^* be the set of such b ∈ A_p; then Hⁿ(G_p(A_p∖A_p^*)) ≤ L_pⁿLⁿ(A_p∖A_p^*) = 0.
 Next apply Simon Ch. 1, 3.6 (SimonGMT simon_theorem_3_6) to the finite Borel regular measure Hⁿ⌞M′ and the set M′∖M′_p, whose Hⁿ⌞M′-measure is finite. It gives Θ*ⁿ(Hⁿ⌞(M′∖M′_p), x) = 0 for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M′_p; let Y_p ⊆ M′_p be the exceptional null set.
 Put Z_j := N ∪ ⋃_p(G_p(A_p∖A_p^*) ∪ Y_p), an Hⁿ-null set, and let x ∈ M′∖Z_j. Then x ∈ M′_p for a unique p, x = G_p(b) with b ∈ A_p^*, and x ∉ Y_p.
 (f) Blow-up. Let L := dG_p(b), which is injective, and L_x := L(ℝⁿ), which has dimension n. Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_R(0), and put R″ := R/min(κ_p, κ(L)). For λ > 0 the similarity η_{x,λ} multiplies Hⁿ by λ^{−n}. So by (d) and the substitution b′ = b + λc,
 ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M′_p)}f dHⁿ = λ^{−n}∫_{M′_p}f((z − x)/λ)dHⁿ(z) = λ^{−n}∫_{A_p}J_p(b′)f((G_p(b′) − G_p(b))/λ)db′ = ∫_{ℝⁿ}h_p(b + λc)f(Δ_λ(c))dc,
 where Δ_λ(c) := (G_p(b + λc) − G_p(b))/λ.
 If h_p(b + λc) ≠ 0, then b + λc ∈ A_p ⊆ S_p, so |Δ_λ(c)| ≥ κ_p|c| ≥ R whenever |c| ≥ R″. Likewise |Lc| ≥ κ(L)|c| ≥ R whenever |c| ≥ R″. Hence
 |∫h_p(b + λc)f(Δ_λ(c))dc − J_p(b)∫_{ℝⁿ}f(Lc)dc| ≤ sup|f|·λ^{−n}∫_{B̄_{λR″}(b)}|h_p − J_p(b)| + J_p(b)∫_{B̄_{R″}(0)}|f(Δ_λ(c)) − f(Lc)|dc,
 and both terms tend to 0 as λ ↓ 0. The first does so by (e). The second does so because Δ_λ(c) → Lc uniformly for |c| ≤ R″ (G_p is differentiable at b) and f is uniformly continuous.
 By the linear area formula, Hⁿ(L(S)) = J_p(b)Lⁿ(S) for all S ⊆ ℝⁿ, so Hⁿ⌞L_x is the image of J_p(b)Lⁿ under L. Hence J_p(b)∫_{ℝⁿ}f(Lc)dc = ∫_{L_x}f dHⁿ.
 Moreover |∫_{η_{x,λ}(M′∖M′_p)}f dHⁿ| ≤ sup|f|·λ^{−n}Hⁿ((M′∖M′_p) ∩ B̄_{λR}(x)) → 0, because x ∉ Y_p.
 Since η_{x,λ} is injective, ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M′)} = ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M′_p)} + ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M′∖M′_p)}. Therefore lim_{λ↓0}∫_{η_{x,λ}(M′)}f dHⁿ = ∫_{L_x}f dHⁿ. The exceptional set Z_j does not depend on f.
 (g) Density bound. Take f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with 0 ≤ f ≤ 1 and f = 1 on B̄_1(0). Then ρ^{−n}Hⁿ(M′ ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = Hⁿ(η_{x,ρ}(M′) ∩ B̄_1(0)) ≤ ∫_{η_{x,ρ}(M′)}f dHⁿ → ∫_{L_x}f dHⁿ < ∞, so Hⁿ(M′ ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ C_xρⁿ for small ρ.

5. Remark 1.8(1): the weighted tangent space of M. Let x ∈ M′∖(Z_j ∪ E_j) with M′ = M^{(j)}, L := L_x = T_xM′ (step 4), and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_R(0). Using x + r y ∈ M for y ∈ η_{x,r}(M) and Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(S)) = r^{-n} Hⁿ(S):
 ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y) θ(x + r y) dHⁿ(y) = θ(x) ∫_{η_{x,r}(M′)} f dHⁿ + ∫_{η_{x,r}(M′)} f(y) (θ(x + r y) − θ(x)) dHⁿ(y) + ∫_{η_{x,r}(M∖M′)} f(y) θ(x + r y) dHⁿ(y).
 The first term tends to θ(x) ∫_L f dHⁿ by step 4. The second is at most sup|f| · sup{|θ(z) − θ(x)| : z ∈ M′ ∩ B̄_{rR}(x)} · r^{-n} Hⁿ(M′ ∩ B̄_{rR}(x)) → 0 by continuity of θ|M′ at x and the bound at the end of step 4. The third is at most sup|f| r^{-n} ∫_{(M∖M′) ∩ B̄_{rR}(x)} θ dHⁿ = sup|f| r^{-n} μ((M∖M′) ∩ B̄_{rR}(x)) → 0 because Θ*ⁿ(μ, M∖M′, x) = 0 (x ∉ E_j). Hence lim_{r↓0} ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y) θ(x + r y) dHⁿ(y) = θ(x) ∫_L f dHⁿ for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), and dim L = n: L is the approximate tangent space of M at x with respect to θ (Definition 1.7).

6. Conclusion. The points of M not covered by step 5 lie in (M∖⋃_j M^{(j)}) ∪ ⋃_j (Z_j ∪ E_j), an Hⁿ-null set. With step 2 this proves the statement for the original M. ∎
proof_key_steps: P < n is vacuous since Hⁿ ≡ 0 on ℝ^P.
Localize to M ∩ W_q with W_q ⊂⊂ U: weighted tangent spaces depend only on M near x, and θ becomes globally integrable.

Remark 1.8(1): Lusin's theorem gives compact sets M^{(j)} ⊆ M of finite measure that exhaust M, with θ|M^{(j)} continuous. Then 3.6 of Ch. 1 gives zero density of θHⁿ⌞(M∖M^{(j)}) at a.e. point of M^{(j)}.

Instead of Lemma 1.2, cut the Lipschitz parametrizations of M^{(j)} into bi-Lipschitz pieces G_p|S_p (Rademacher, null critical images, approximately linear partition). Disjointify to M′_p = G_p(A_p) and use the injective area formula.

Let x = G_p(b), where b is a Lebesgue point of 1_{A_p}J_p and M′∖M′_p has zero density at x. Then the blow-ups of M^{(j)} at x converge to the plane dG_p(b)(ℝⁿ) (linear area formula), and Hⁿ(M^{(j)} ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ C_xρⁿ.
The unweighted tangent of M^{(j)}, continuity of θ|M^{(j)} and zero density of the rest give the weighted tangent of M at x. All exceptional sets are countably many Hⁿ-null sets.

audit.reason: Localization and Lusin exhaustion supply finite compact pieces. The verified derivative partition, critical-image theorem and area formulas justify the bi-Lipschitz decomposition and blow-up calculation. Differentiation and zero density of the remaining pieces control both errors, uniformly in the choice of test function's exceptional set. The proof establishes the exact weighted tangent definition.
